newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up on strength in properties.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up on strength in properties.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed higher on Monday, due chiefly to positive local sentiment in the longer-term outlook for major property developers, brokers said.
"There was less selling and a more positive stance from locally-based institutions," said Glenn Lesko, head of equities trading at HG Asia.
The Hang Seng Index gained 84.86 points to close at 12,626.04 after hitting a high for the day of 12,711.31 during a surprisingly strong rebound in the morning session.
Volume in index stocks dropped off again on Monday, Lesko added.
Brokers said trading in China-related red chips continued to dominate market activity.
While blue chips remained on top of the turnover chart, nine of the top 20 most-actively traded issues were red chips and H-shares, with only one Hong Kong-based second line issue making the list.
The property sector led the rebound, outperforming the rest of the blue chips. Sun Hung Kai Properties led the way with a jump of HK$1.50 to HK$79.75.
Cheung Kong added HK$1.00 to HK$68.25, but Swire Pacific was one of the biggest net losers, falling HK$0.50 to HK$58.25.
H-shares came under selling pressure chiefly due to the worse than expected results from Yizheng Chemical Fibre and Northeast Electrical Transmission.
Yizheng closed HK$0.07 lower at HK$1.32 on thin turnover of HK$13.08 million after reporting an 82 percent fall in 1996 earnings to 215.65 million yuan.
Northeast Electrical also slid HK$0.07 to HK$1.39 after it reported a 49 percent fall in 1996 earnings.
But selected red chips tended firmer with Shanghai Industrial up HK$0.20 at HK$40.70 and China Resources up HK$0.50 at HK$20.15.
The market ended on a firm note bolstered by a jump in the April Hang Seng Index future contract of 90 points to 12,625.
In the coming one to two weeks, the index should trade in a range of 12,360 to 12,900, said chartist Ted Chen of Technical Data. "The strategy for this year is to buy on dips," said Chen.
Brokers also said Monday's arrival of an advance party of Chinese soldiers in Hong Kong to prepare for the territory's return to China later this year had no effect on the market.
